blocks.x: Field-service dispatch on governed agents — truck rolls down 22% and first-visit resolution up 17 points
a cable operator whose customer promise met its dispatch board every morning and lost. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline month measured the board: 31% of truck rolls resolving at the tap (not the customer), average 3.4 jobs per tech per day, and the no-problem-at-premises rate quietly funded by the appointment book.
Dispatch ran on territory and intuition. Network telemetry existed but dispatch never read it; the tech arrived, reproduced nothing, and rebooked.

We rebuilt dispatch as governed agents: every appointment pre-screened against network telemetry and device health, remote-resolution attempts logged before any truck moves, tech skill and parts matched to predicted fault, and the exception queue routing genuinely ambiguous cases to humans. The appointment book started believing the network.
